description:
Makes the LDPC batch decoder take the AVX2 lane backend when the build and the host provide it, with the portable backend and the single-frame route as tested fallbacks.

## Background

The batch soft-decoder trait of `gf2-coding` decodes a batch of LLR frames into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order. Its LDPC implementer, the LDPC batch decoder, decodes fixed waves of eight lanes with per-frame termination, routes a wave to the lane kernels or to the single-frame decoder by the decode selectors of the coding tuning section, and returns each frame's result equal to the single-frame decoder's bit for bit as `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states. `gf2-kernels-simd` publishes an AVX2 backend of the lane kernel bundle through runtime detection, bit-identical to the portable backend. The suite `ldpc_batch_contract` holds a route to the single-frame decoder at the posterior level.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With the `simd` cargo feature of `gf2-coding` and AVX2 detected at run time, the lane route runs the AVX2 backend; without either it runs the portable backend; the route reporter names the backend.
- [hard] REQ-02: The posterior-level suite and the shared batch contract function pass on the AVX2 backend, on the portable backend and on the single-frame route in one test binary, and a test binary built without `simd` pins the portable backend.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test-only process-global backend override, if one exists, is held under a mutex for the whole toggle-execute-observe-restore section.
- [hard] REQ-04: The steady-state decode on the AVX2 backend performs no allocation, reallocation or deallocation.
- [hard] REQ-05: Rustdoc of the LDPC batch decoder names the cargo feature and the runtime capability that select the AVX2 backend.
title: Route LDPC batch decoding to the AVX2 lanes by capability
